takeaway: Hot, breezy and mostly dry through the weekend, near 34–35°C in Nicoya. Surf stays offshore every morning through Monday, with the strongest trade winds Saturday night and Sunday, and a bigger southwest swell (6–8 ft at 16 seconds) Saturday into Sunday night. The bigger change is next week: the models are wetter for the early-November rain spell, which now runs about Tuesday Nov 3 through Thursday Nov 5, with Wednesday and Thursday the wettest days. Afternoons turn onshore as the trades fade. No tropical storm threat, but the prolonged-rain watch moves up a notch.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Fri–Sun, Oct 30–Nov 1)
periods.pattern: Costa Rica's weather service (IMN) calls for few clouds and gusty winds on the North Pacific today, with moderate breezes into the afternoon. Nicoya's high is about 34.5°C with a low near 21°C, and Liberia about 34°C. IMN gives a chance of scattered afternoon showers or an isolated storm toward the southern end of the Nicoya Peninsula today. Its new weekly outlook adds more moisture from Saturday, with scattered afternoon showers possible over the Nicoya Peninsula, while most of the North Pacific stays dry. The models keep Nosara at about 0–2 mm today and Saturday and about 2–6 mm on Sunday.
periods.implications: Good outdoor days, especially mornings. Bring water for the heat. From Saturday an afternoon shower is a bit more likely than earlier in the week, but most hours stay dry.
periods.confidence: High on mostly dry, hot and breezy. Moderate on whether a weekend afternoon shower reaches Nosara.

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Mon Nov 2 – Thu Nov 5)
periods.pattern: Monday is still breezy and mostly dry, about 4–6 mm in the model averages. IMN expects a weak tropical wave to cross early in the week. From Tuesday the trade winds fade and the shower belt that has been sitting south of Costa Rica moves north over Nicoya, with light southwest to west winds pushing up from the south by Wednesday and Thursday. Every model average puts about 16–22 mm (two-thirds to three-quarters of an inch) at Nosara on Tuesday. The European average then shows about 29 mm on Wednesday and 35 mm on Thursday, and the American and AI averages about 16–22 mm a day. This is Pacific-side rain, not Caribbean.
periods.implications: Plan outdoor things for Monday or earlier. Keep Tuesday through Thursday flexible: expect afternoon and evening downpours with storms, and possibly a longer rainy stretch on Wednesday or Thursday. Watch for muddy roads and fast-rising creeks.
periods.confidence: High on Monday staying mostly dry. Moderate to high on Nov 3–5 turning wet. Low on exact amounts.

periods.label: Days 8–15 (Fri Nov 6 – Fri Nov 13)
periods.pattern: Rain eases after Nov 5–6, but not all at once. The European average still has about 16 mm around Nov 7, then drops to 3–4 mm a day for Nov 9–13. The American average keeps light showers, about 6–9 mm a day around Nov 7–9 and about 4 mm by Nov 11–13. The trade winds look to return over Nicaragua around Nov 9–11. IMN's long-range outlook (issued Oct 26) still calls for drier than normal weather through Nov 22, with the dry season settling in on the North Pacific in early November.
periods.implications: Expect a gradual dry-out through the second week of November, with a stray shower still possible. A better stretch for plans is likely from about Nov 9 onward.
periods.confidence: Moderate on drying out after Nov 7. Low on timing and amounts.

surfWinds.regime: Caribbean trades, so it's offshore at Nosara every morning through Monday. Moderate today, strongest Saturday night and Sunday. The trades fade from Tuesday, and Nov 3–6 favors light winds early and onshore or side-on afternoons from the Pacific side.
surfWinds.detail: The Papagayo marine forecast (issued 2:43 a.m. Costa Rica time) has northeast to east winds of 15–20 knots near the coast today and tonight and 20–25 knots out in the Gulf of Papagayo, with 5–7 ft at 15 seconds. Saturday is northeast 15–20 knots with a 6–8 ft southwest swell at 16 seconds. Saturday night and Sunday firm up to 20–25 knots in the gulf (Sunday 20–25 across the area), still 6–8 ft at 15–16 seconds. Monday eases to northeast 15–20 with 5–7 ft, then east 10–15 Monday night and east 10 Tuesday with 4–6 ft at 14 seconds. By Tuesday night it's southeast 10, the trades letting go. One caution: the waters just south of the peninsula go from calm and variable today to west breezes of about 10 knots from Saturday afternoon and southwest 10–15 knots from Monday night. Nosara sits near that edge, so afternoons can go side-on or onshore sooner than farther north. Nicaragua looks offshore all day through Monday, a good sign for clean Nosara mornings, but Nosara won't necessarily hold offshore all day.
surfWinds.bestWindows: This morning and Saturday morning for the 15–16-second swell in moderate offshore wind. Sunday and Monday mornings have the biggest swell but the strongest trades, so go at first light before it gets bumpy and hard to paddle into. Long-period sets come bigger and less often than the average height suggests, and rip currents run stronger. From Tuesday, early mornings are the only shot at clean conditions, with onshore afternoons and showers through Thursday.
surfWinds.confidence: High on offshore mornings through Monday. Moderate on how long afternoons hold. Moderate to high on the trades fading from Tuesday.

gyreWatch.status: Watch only, nudged up from low to low-to-moderate. No slow-spinning low is forecast, but the Nov 3–5 rain spell looks wetter and a day longer than yesterday.
gyreWatch.possibleTiming: Tuesday Nov 3 through Thursday Nov 5, possibly lingering to Nov 7.
gyreWatch.supporting: All the model averages bring the shower belt north over Nicoya on Nov 3–5, and the European average is clearly wetter than yesterday (about 29–35 mm a day on Nov 4–5, up from 16–22). The regular European run shows a broad band of southwest winds just south of Costa Rica by Thursday Nov 5, the kind of moist Pacific feed that drives temporales. IMN expects a weak tropical wave early next week. NOAA's tropics outlook (Oct 27) says weaker easterly winds south of Mexico in the Nov 4–17 window could briefly favor a late-season East Pacific storm.
gyreWatch.conflicting: No model average shows a closed low parked off Costa Rica, and the southwest winds stay mostly south of the country. The trades return over Nicaragua around Nov 9–11, which cuts the wet spell short. IMN's long-range outlook still expects drier than normal through Nov 22. The U.S. hurricane center expects nothing near Central America in the next week; its only East Pacific area is far southeast of Hawaii (30% in 7 days), and nothing is expected in the Caribbean. Tropical Storm Vance has dropped out of the outlook.

whatChanged: The early-November rain spell got wetter and a day longer: the European average now peaks at about 29–35 mm on Nov 4–5, up from 16–22 mm, and keeps about 16 mm around Nov 7. The trades firm up a bit more this weekend, now 20–25 knots in the Gulf of Papagayo Saturday night and Sunday. IMN's new weekly outlook (Oct 29–Nov 4) adds scattered afternoon showers over the Nicoya Peninsula from Saturday and a weak tropical wave early next week. Today's IMN shower chance shifts to the southern end of the peninsula. Tropical Storm Vance is gone from the hurricane center's outlook. No new IMN notices since Oct 25.
practical: Surf early every morning through Monday, ideally at first light on Sunday and Monday when the trades are strongest and the swell is biggest. Watch for stronger rip currents. Days stay hot and mostly sunny through Monday, with a small chance of an afternoon shower from Saturday. Move outdoor plans to the weekend or Monday and keep Tuesday through Thursday (Nov 3–5) flexible for afternoon and evening downpours. No tropical storm threat to Costa Rica.
